decisive_items: Biopsy of posterior left pleural thickening showed CD5+, CD10−, non-germinal center B-cell type
Fluorescence in situ hybridization analysis: negative for Myc, BCL6, t(14;18)/IGH-BCL2, and t(11;14)/CCND1-IGH gene rearrangements
Avid irregular enhancement within the right cavernous sinus and enlargement of the right side compared with the left
response.rationale: R4 is champion because the pleural biopsy is definitive for a CD5+ CD10− non-germinal center B-cell lymphoma, and the FISH pattern excludes mantle-cell and high-grade rearrangements; the right cavernous sinus enhancement with CN III/VI palsies is best explained as lymphomatous involvement. R7 captures the local anatomy but is an exclusion diagnosis and cannot account for the systemic biopsy-proven lymphoma.

rejected.why: Sinus air-fluid levels are incidental and cannot explain cavernous sinus enhancement, systemic lymphadenopathy, or the B-cell lymphoma biopsy.
Prostate cancer history and pleural mass are present, but the biopsy phenotype is B-cell lymphoma, not metastatic adenocarcinoma.
Lymphadenopathy and sinus opacification are nonspecific; biopsy shows lymphoma, not non-caseating granulomas, and cavernous sinus involvement is atypical.
Temporal headache and photosensitivity are nonspecific; normal ESR/CRP and the absence of visual ischemic complications plus biopsy-proven lymphoma make GCA unlikely.
